content:
Facts The spouse and children of a predeceased sister of the testatrix challenged a will benefiting the testatrix’s siblings, alleging nullity and infringement of their inheritance rights, and sought monetary reinstatement and damages.
Legal framework
Articles 536, 553–564, 591, 624 ICC on forced heirs, reduction, acceptance with benefit of inventory, testamentary incapacity and error; Articles 467–468 ICC on representation; Articles 96 and 100 CPC on aggravated liability and standing.
Interpretative issue
Whether relatives succeeding by representation to a sibling of the deceased qualify as forced heirs entitled to bring an action for reduction, and whether generic pleas of testamentary nullity can be expanded into distinct grounds of invalidity at a later stage.
Principle applied
Only persons expressly designated by law as forced heirs may bring an action for reduction; siblings of the deceased are not forced heirs, and their descendants succeeding by representation lack standing to claim infringement of reserved shares. In such cases, prior acceptance of the inheritance with benefit of inventory is also required. Generic allegations of testamentary nullity do not encompass distinct grounds such as incapacity or error, which, if not timely and specifically pleaded, constitute an inadmissible mutatio libelli. The manifest groundlessness of an action brought without due legal diligence justifies a finding of reckless litigation and the award of aggravated liability damages under Article 96 CPC.
